guide.title: Garrosh's Overview
guide.text:
Garrosh is a Tank who becomes more difficult to kill
the closer he is to death because of how his Trait, Armor Up, works.
Arguably, one of Garrosh's strongest mechanics is his ability to displace
enemy Heroes over relatively large distances via Wrecking Ball,
something that will immensely impact the outcome of a team fight
and put a lot of pressure on the enemy team while laning.

guide.title: Garrosh's Strengths and Weaknesses
guide.text:
Strengths
Incredibly durable via Armor Up, becomes harder to kill the closer he is to death
Can reposition enemies or allies with Wrecking Ball and Into the Fray
Very strong playmaker
Provides a reliable frontline, with excellent damage mitigation
Very high skill ceiling
Weaknesses
Rather poor damage output, especially during the late game
Can be easily kited, particularly by Ranged Assassins
Absolutely no method of increasing mobility; relies entirely on Abilities and crowd-control to reach his desired target
Very complex Hero, requires mastery of many subtle nuances to be most effective

guide.title: Garrosh's Synergies and Counters
guide.text:
Garrosh synergizes with
If you want to get more value from Garrosh, pair him with Heroes who can follow up
his engage with crowd control (such as Deckard Cain)
and/or burst damage (for example Kael'thas).
Garrosh does not have a strong engage from the distance,
so he likes to play in team with Heroes who have access to powerful Abiliities to help him engage
(like Hanzo with Dragon's Arrow).
Compensate his lack of mobility (for example with Speed Barrier
by Zarya) and Garrosh will become even more scary to play against
as he will be able to just walk towards enemy Heroes for
catching them with Wrecking Ball.
Garrosh is countered by
Garrosh does not like to face Heroes who have access to
on-demand Unstoppable effects
(such as Johanna) because Wrecking Ball
will not target them but the second nearest target in range.
If these Heroes get thrown instead of an ally to peel for them,
then they can use that defensive Ability to walk out uncontested,
unless crowd controlled to death.
Heroes who can kite him away from their team (for example Lunara)
are great Garrosh's counters, however, keep in mind that he can occasionally mitigate this
by activating Indomitable at Level 4.
Considering that Garrosh relies on Armor to mitigate incoming damage,
he is weak to percent-based damage (like Leoric) and
effects that reduce Armor (for example Sylvanas with
Overwhelming Affliction at Level 1).
Another way to counter Garrosh is using tools to help allied Heroes
survive burst damage (such as Force of Will by Medivh)
and/or move them out of danger (like Leap of Faith by Anduin).

guide.title: Garrosh's Maps
guide.text:
Garrosh's stronger maps
Garrosh's average maps
Garrosh's weaker maps
Garrosh thrives in situations where his enemies are forced to
clump together in groups. This is because most of his Abilities,
(notably Groundbreaker and Warlord's Challenge)
gain value when they are able to strike
more than one target. Maps with many narrow choke points
provide Garrosh a playground of opportunities to catch out his enemies.
Wrecking Ball is a lot of fun on Maps with lots of
terrain as Garrosh can use it to completely isolate an enemy Hero away from their allies
by flipping them over impassable terrain or Structure into his team.

guide.title: Garrosh's Tips and Tricks
guide.text:
Armor Up gives Garrosh an impressive amount of damage mitigation while at low Health, allowing him to stay in combat longer than most other Heroes.
Groundbreaker can be used to Stun an enemy Hero before or after throwing them with Wrecking Ball.
Bloodthirst's self-sustain is most effective after Garrosh has suffered damage as it heals for a percentage of his missing Health.
Remember that Wrecking Ball is not a targeted Ability and will automatically target the closest non-Unstoppable Hero (including Misha), Clone, Minion, or Mercenary within range. Summons and Monsters are invalid targets.
Due to the small radius of Warlord's Challenge, it will sometimes be difficult to strike multiple Heroes with it. It will often times be worth using Warlord's Challenge on a single Hero should it help secure a kill and ensure a numbers advantage for Garrosh's team.
To play around Abilities that give mobility or Unstoppable, you can use Wrecking Ball and immediately cast Warlord's Challenge before the target enemy Hero lands.
See our Abilities page for further information »

guide.title: Garrosh's Role in the Current Meta
guide.text:
Garrosh is a great Hero choice for teams that are in need of a strong frontline
and happen to lack a reliable source of crowd control.
As a consequence, he works best with Heroes who are able to follow up on his
engage with additional crowd control
and especially large amounts of burst damage.

abilities.title: Garrosh's Tips and Tricks
abilities.text:
Armor Up gives Garrosh an impressive amount of damage mitigation while at low Health, allowing him to stay in combat longer than most other Heroes.
Groundbreaker can be used to Stun an enemy Hero before or after throwing them with Wrecking Ball.
Bloodthirst's self-sustain is most effective after Garrosh has suffered damage as it heals for a percentage of his missing Health.
Remember that Wrecking Ball is not a targeted Ability and will automatically target the closest non-Unstoppable Hero (including Misha), Clone, Minion, or Mercenary within range. Summons and Monsters are invalid targets.
Due to the small radius of Warlord's Challenge, it will sometimes be difficult to strike multiple Heroes with it. It will often times be worth using Warlord's Challenge on a single Hero should it help secure a kill and ensure a numbers advantage for Garrosh's team.
To play around Abilities that give mobility or Unstoppable, you can use Wrecking Ball and immediately cast Warlord's Challenge before the target enemy Hero lands.

abilities.title: Groundbreaker
abilities.text:
Groundbreaker
(Q)
Garrosh
Mana: 40
Cooldown: 8 seconds
Deal 81 (+4% per level) damage to enemies in an area. Heroes hit on the outer edge are Stunned for 0.5 seconds and then Slowed by 40% for 2 seconds.
Groundbreaker deals some damage to all enemies in
its whole area and briefly Stuns and then Slows
all enemy Heroes on its edge. Since it has a short delay from
when it is cast to when the Ability strikes, you will have to somewhat
anticipate the movements of the enemy Heroes to catch them on the outer area.
Based on the situation, it can be used to engage enemy Heroes,
peel for allied Heroes, or interrupt
impactful channeled Abiliites (such as the powerful
Mosh Pit by E.T.C. or the useful
Drain Life by Gul'dan).

abilities.title: Bloodthirst
abilities.text:
Bloodthirst
(W)
Garrosh
Mana: 55
Cooldown: 12 seconds
Deal 156 (+4% per level) damage to an enemy and heal for 10% of Garrosh's missing Health. Healing is increased by 100% against Heroes.
Bloodthirst is an incredibly important tool Garrosh will utilize
for self-sustain and staying power throughout all phases of a match.
It is crucial to note that the amount Garrosh will heal from Bloodthirst is based off of
his missing Health when the Ability is cast. This means that the less Health Garrosh has,
the more value he will receive from Bloodthirst. Also, the healing received from Bloodthirst is doubled
when the Ability used against an enemy Hero. Due to the rather long cooldown of Bloodthirst (12 seconds),
it is vital Garrosh uses this Ability wisely. It may sometimes be advantageous for Garrosh to
wait until he has taken a significant amount of damage to cast Bloodthirst as this will grant
him significantly more Health than if he had used it right at the beginning of a trade.

abilities.title: Wrecking Ball
abilities.text:
Wrecking Ball
(E)
Garrosh
Mana: 60
Cooldown: 16 seconds
Throw a nearby enemy Hero, Minion, or Mercenary to the target location, dealing 91 (+4% per level) damage to enemies near the impact and Slowing them by 30% for 2.5 seconds.
Wrecking Ball is a powerful Ability
featuring a displacement effect
that Garrosh can use both offensively and defensively.
Since this Ability works as a Stun,
you can use it to interrupt both
stationary (such as Dark Conversion by Mal'Ganis)
and mobile channeled Abilities
(for example Unrelenting Strikes by Qhira),
given who is casting them is within range.
In the early game,
Garrosh can flank to surprise enemy Heroes with a
sudden close-range engage that will allow him to start with
Wrecking Ball—usually towards your
team before unlocking Warlord's Challenge and towards
the enemy team after that—and then follow-up with
Groundbreaker.
Sometimes you can use
Groundbreaker to Slow an enemy Hero and then cast
Wrecking Ball on them as soon as you get in range.
In some situations you may also need to use Groundbreaker
to peel away an enemy Hero from a teammate in danger.
Keep in mind that this Ability will always target the closest enemy Hero, Minion,
or Mercenary within 2.25 range at the moment of its cast. The closest valid enemy will
have a red Horde symbol on them. Unstoppable enemies are ignored,
meaning that Garrosh will look for the next closest valid target after them.
The position of your mouse cursor will determine where the target will be
thrown by this Ability, allowing you to
reposition the closest enemy to a specific location within 6 range.
You can use this unique effect to throw enemy Heroes into dangerous spots
to help your teammates connect their Abilities (notably Steel Trap by Junkrat).
In some situations, you can also throw enemy Heroes on the spot, to use Wrecking Ball
as a pseudo-Stun in order to not mess up your teammates' follow up.

abilities.title: Warlord's Challenge
abilities.text:
In this section we discuss how this Heroic Ability works and give some tips on how to use it.
If you are looking for a detailed explanation on when and why you should pick it,
check out the dedicated section in the Talent Build page.
Warlord's Challenge
(R)
Garrosh
Heroic
Mana: 40
Cooldown: 50 seconds
Silence nearby Heroes and force them to attack Garrosh for 2 seconds.
Warlord's Challenge is a Heroic Ability
which provides a powerful crowd control effect
in the form of Taunt. Once cast, all enemies caught
within a small radius around Garrosh will become Silenced
and forced to hit Garrosh with their Basic Attacks for 2 seconds.
Due to his lack of mobility or
gap closer, Garrosh will likely have to rely on a well
placed Groundbreaker in order to get in close
enough to successfully cast Warlord's Challenge.

Warlord's Challenge can be used to set up cataclysmic Ability combos, especially
when Garrosh is teamed up with Assassins who can
deal large amounts of burst damage.
Although Warlord's Challenge can
Taunt all enemy Heroes found within its radius,
Garrosh should not be afraid to cast it on a single target should
it help secure a kill for his team. In Heroes of the Storm, being able to gain
a numerical advantage over the enemy team (especially
in the late game) will often times
allow your team to build an advantage.
When under the Taunt effect, Heroes who are too
far from Garrosh will move towards him. This means that you can walk
backwards right after using Warlord's Challenge
to move enemy Heroes towards your team. This trick works best against
melee Heroes as they have a short Attack Range.

abilities.title: Decimate
abilities.text:
In this section we discuss how this Heroic Ability works and give some tips on how to use it.
If you are looking for a detailed explanation on when and why you should pick it,
check out the dedicated section in the Talent Build page.
Decimate
(R)
Garrosh
Heroic
Mana: 25
Charges: 3
Recharge Time: 8 seconds
Deal 50 (+4% per level) damage to nearby enemies and Slow them by 40% for 1.5 seconds. Deals 100% more damage to Heroes, and each Hero hit reduces the cooldown by 1 second.
Stores up to 3 charges.
Decimate is a Heroic Ability with multiple charges
that focuses more on sustain damage, doubled against enemy Heroes,
and crowd control in the form of a Slow.
Both effects are area of effect.
You can hold up to 3 charges of Decimate
and each charge will take 8 seconds to regenerate, however, each Hero
hit will reduce its cooldown by 1 second. Assuming that Garrosh is able to
hit the entire enemy team with a single cast of Decimate, the remaining cooldown
of the next charge of Decimate will be brought down to 3 seconds.

abilities.title: Armor Up
abilities.text:
Armor Up
(D)
Garrosh
Passive
Garrosh gains 1 Armor for every 2% of maximum Health missing.
Armor Up is Garrosh's foremost source of damage mitigation
and one of the primary factors behind his role as a main tank.
The mechanic is simple, the more Health Garrosh is missing, the more Armor he is granted.
It is important to note that this Armor reduces the damage Garrosh receives from all
sources, including both Basic Attacks and Abilities. Garrosh will be granted 1 Armor for
every 2% of Health he is missing, meaning that Garrosh will mitigate almost half of the
damage he receives when at very low Health.
Although Armor Up is strongest when Garrosh
is near death, that does not mean he should be reckless with his positioning during fights
and skirmishes. Heavy focus-fire from the enemy team will still
bring down Garrosh very quickly despite his durability. Garrosh's Armor can be always
easily viewed by looking at the number under the shield directly to the right of his
Health Bar. This number is useful to track as some of his Abilities and Talents will be
dependent on his current Armor value.

abilities.title: Into the Fray
abilities.text:
Into the Fray
(1)
Garrosh
Activate to throw a nearby ally and grant them 20 Armor for 3 seconds. Deals 91 (+4% per level) damage to nearby enemies upon impact and Slows them by 30% for 2.5 seconds.
While in flight, allied Heroes are Unstoppable.
Into the Fray is a baseline Active Ability
which can be used to displace allies
and give them some Armor for a few seconds.
While in the air, they become Unstoppable
and they cannot cast Abilities due to being dazed.
Upon landing, they deal damage to all enemies nearby
and Slow them by a small amount.
You can use it either defensively or offensively.
Using it defensively means to reposition an allied Hero
away from enemy Heroes so that they can survive,
give them Unstoppable
as a way to deny a dangerous Ability (for example
Temporal Loop by Chromie),
or give them Armor to mitigate
a powerful shot (such as Pyroblast
by Kael'thas).
Using it offensively means to help an allied melee Hero
(like Kerrigan) engage,
or to throw an allied Minion on an enemy Hero as a way of
dealing lethal damage to them or Slowing
them from the distance.

Warbreaker after Quest completion and about the same
as Unrivaled Strength).

talent_pages.title: Level 4 Talents for Garrosh
talent_pages.text:
?
In For the Kill
(Level 4)
Garrosh
Increase Bloodthirst's damage against non-Heroes by 100%. Killing enemies with Bloodthirst resets its cooldown and refunds its Mana cost.
In For the Kill is a decent Talent that increases the damage
dealt by Bloodthirst on non-Heroes. Furthermore, when
Bloodthirst is used to deal lethal damage to an enemy,
it resets its cooldown and refunds its Mana cost.
We find this Talent useful to clear Minions and Monsters who have low maximum Health
(for example the Skeletal Defenders on Infernal Shrines) as you will easily get
the cooldown reset when using Bloodthirst on them.
You should pick this Talent when you have no Healer,
when you are playing Garrosh as Offlaner, or
when your team needs more waveclear.
?
Thirst for Battle
(Level 4)
Garrosh
Basic Attacks against Heroes reduce the cooldown of Bloodthirst by 2 seconds.
Thirst for Battle is a good Talent that reduces the cooldown of
Bloodthirst when hitting enemy Heroes with Basic Attacks.
The reduced cooldown of Bloodthirst will slightly increase your damage output
and survivability, especially if combined with Bloodcraze at Level 13
and Seasoned Soldier at Level 16.
✔
Indomitable
(Level 4)
Garrosh
Cooldown: 40 seconds
Activate to become Unstoppable for 1.5 seconds.
Indomitable is a strong Talent that gives yourself
Unstoppable for 1.5 seconds on a relatively short cooldown,
something that is extremely good for playing around kite
when you want to engage.
Active it when you expect a Stun or Silence to hit you
(because they stop you from casting Abilities) or use it when you are already affected by a Root
or Slow (because they do not stop you from casting Abilities).
When playing against Diablo, you can activate Indomitable
right after using Wrecking Ball on him so that he cannot
get out by using Shadow Charge on you.

talent_pages.title: Level 7 Talents for Garrosh
talent_pages.text:
?
Intimidation
(Level 7)
Garrosh
Groundbreaker reduces the Attack Speed of Heroes hit by 30% for 4 seconds.
Intimidation is a situational Talent that
allows you to reduce the Attack Speed of enemy Heroes hit
with either the inner or outer area of Groundbreaker,
so it does not matter if you do not Stun them in the process.
✔
Oppressor
(Level 7)
Garrosh
Basic Attacks and Bloodthirst against Heroes reduce the target's Spell Power by 25% for 2.5 seconds.
Oppressor is a strong Talent that makes your Basic Attacks
and Bloodthirst apply a debuff to enemy Heroes
which reduces their damage and healing done with Abilities.
?
Lok-tar ogar!
(Level 7)
Garrosh
Increase Into the Fray's Armor by 20. Hitting enemy Heroes with Into the Fray reduces its cooldown by 12 seconds.
Lok-tar ogar! is an extremely situational Talent that
increases the Armor provided by Into the Fray
and reduces its cooldown by a dozen of seconds for each enemy Hero hit
with the displaced ally.
The problem with using Into the Fray
aggressively is that you will not have it for defensive usage
for many seconds, unless you hit 3 enemy Heroes with it
and reduce its cooldown down to 10 seconds as a consequence.
You can use the extra Armor provided by
this Talent to save allied Heroes from burst damage
(such as Pyroblast by Kael'thas)
or dive (for example Zeratul).

talent_pages.title: Level 10 Talents for Garrosh
talent_pages.text:
In this section we discuss when and why to pick a given Heroic Ability.
If you want to read how they work in detail and/or you are looking for some tips on how to use them,
check them out on the Abilities and Strategy page.
?
Warlord's Challenge
(Level 10)
Garrosh
Mana: 40
Cooldown: 50 seconds
Silence nearby Heroes and force them to attack Garrosh for 2 seconds.
Warlord's Challenge is a good Heroic Ability
which provides a powerful area of effect
crowd control. Once cast, all enemy Heroes caught within
a small radius around Garrosh will be Taunted for a short while.
Pick this Heroic Ability when your team needs crowd control
to lock enemy Heroes down for securing kills, to peel from
dive, or to have an interrupt
for powerful channeled Abilities. Ideally,
you should have a secondary engage in team.
✔
Decimate
(Level 10)
Garrosh
Mana: 25
Charges: 3
Recharge Time: 8 seconds
Deal 50 (+4% per level) damage to nearby enemies and Slow them by 40% for 1.5 seconds. Deals 100% more damage to Heroes, and each Hero hit reduces the cooldown by 1 second.
Stores up to 3 charges.
Decimate is a strong Heroic Ability which provides
area of effect sustain damage.
Thanks to its relatively low cooldown, it can also be used for
waveclear when needed.
Pick this Heroic Ability to increase your threat range, so that
you can engage from a higher distance than usual.
This way you can punish enemy Heroes who step too close and/or make up for
the lack of a secondary engage in team.

talent_pages.title: Level 13 Talents for Garrosh
talent_pages.text:
?
Defensive Measures
(Level 13)
Garrosh
If Groundbreaker Stuns a Hero, Garrosh gains a 350 (+4% per level) Shield for 6 seconds.
Defensive Measures is a strong Talent that protects Garrosh
with a Shield when hitting enemy Heroes with the outer area of Groundbreaker,
so you need to Stun them to make it work.
The bonus Shield provided allows Garrosh to become an
even stronger frontline Hero and makes him even harder
to burst down.
Defensive Measures synergizes with Warbreaker at Level 1
because the small cooldown reduction it provides to Groundbreaker
increases the uptime potential of the bonus Shield.
Shields are amplified by the damage mitigation provided by Armor Up,
meaning that Defensive Measures will be more effective while Garrosh has low Health.
✔
Bloodcraze
(Level 13)
Garrosh
When hitting a Hero, Bloodthirst heals for an additional 15% of Garrosh's maximum Health over 4 seconds.
Bloodcraze is a good Talent that tends to be outclassed by
Defensive Measures as a defensive Level 13 Talent.
However, Bloodcraze is still considered situational as it may be advantageous
to Garrosh against highly mobile melee targets who are difficult to hit
with casts of Groundbreaker (such as Illidan).
Rather than losing
out completely on the benefits of Defensive Measures by not being able to Stun
an enemy Hero with Groundbreaker, Garrosh may still receive the additional
passive Healing granted by his targeted Basic Ability Bloodthirst.
?
Double Up
(Level 13)
Garrosh
Cooldown: 30 seconds
Armor Up can be activated to increase its Armor bonus by 100% for 5 seconds.
Double Up is a situational Talent that can be manually activated to increase the
damage mitigation provided by Armor Up for a few seconds.
The 100% bonus Armor can come in clutch, preventing Garrosh from being taken
down especially if he finds himself under heavy fire without the immediate
assistance of his team. Remember that Armor cannot go above or below 75.
As a consequence, this Talent will give its maximum value when Garrosh has about 30% maximum Health or less.

talent_pages.title: Level 16 Talents for Garrosh
talent_pages.text:
?
Mortal Combo
(Level 16)
Garrosh
Hitting a Hero with Groundbreaker's Stun and throwing them with Wrecking Ball within 3 seconds reduces Wrecking Ball's cooldown by 10 seconds, regardless of order.
Mortal Combo is a good Talent that can set up
some ridiculously crippling crowd-control
combos.
Throwing an enemy Hero with Wrecking Ball
after Stunning them with Groundbreaker will
result in the two Abilities being ready to use again at around the same time,
allowing you to reposition enemy Heroes every 8 seconds—6 seconds
with Warbreaker at Level 1—while fighting.
When you have Mortal Combo at Level 16
and Titanic Might at Level 20,
when catching 2 enemy Heroes with Wrecking Ball
and hitting them with Groundbreaker right after,
you will be able to throw them on the spot 2 more times.
Unrivaled Strength at Level 1 increases the damage done this way.
?
Earthshaker
(Level 16)
Garrosh
Wrecking Ball Stuns enemies near the impact area for 0.5 seconds.
Earthshaker is a good Talent that
will cause whatever enemy Hero you throw with
Wrecking Ball to be Stunned upon their landing
and Stun all enemies who are in that area.
You can also throw an enemy towards an enemy Hero
to use this Talent as a ranged Stun. This move can be
useful to interrupt enemies attempting
to channel a powerful Ability (for example
Holy Word: Salvation by Anduin)
and/or to group two or more enemy Heroes for Warlord's Challenge.
✔
Seasoned Soldier
(Level 16)
Garrosh
Gain 5% maximum Health, increase Groundbreaker's Slow duration by 1 second, and Bloodthirst gains an additional charge.
Seasoned Soldier is a strong Talent that passively
increases Garrosh's maximum Health by 103 (+4% per level), boosts the Slow duration
of Groundbreaker from 2 to 3 seconds, and provides an
additional charge of Bloodthirst.
While the first and second effects are not that impactful, the third effect is a huge
boost to Garrosh's survivability. You can empower this Talent by combining it with
Thirst for Battle at Level 4 and/or Bloodcraze at Level 13.

talent_pages.title: Level 20 Talents for Garrosh
talent_pages.text:
?
Death Wish
(Level 20)
Garrosh
Increase the duration of Warlord's Challenge by 0.5 seconds. If an enemy Hero is killed while Taunted by Warlord's Challenge, its cooldown is reduced by 45 seconds.
Death Wish is a situational Talent that allows Garrosh to
reset the cooldown of Warlord's Challenge after taking
down an enemy Hero while also increasing the Taunt duration
from 2 to 2.5 seconds.
You should consider picking this Talent when your team's strategy involves
killing an isolated enemy Hero using Abilities that split their damage evenly
on all Heroes hit (for example Seven-Sided Strike
by Kharazim).
✔
Deadly Calm
(Level 20)
Garrosh
Heroes hit by Decimate deal 40% less damage for 3 seconds.
Deadly Calm is a strong Talent that almost halves the damage
done by enemy Heroes hit by Decimate for a few seconds.
The fact that Decimate has multiple charges and a cooldown reduction component
allows you to potentially keep the debuff active
for a dozen of seconds on multiple enemy Heroes within range.
Avoid using multiple charges on the same
enemy Heroes in quick succession because the second damage reduction effect will not stack
with the first one, but only refresh its duration.
?
Titanic Might
(Level 20)
Garrosh
Wrecking Ball now throws the 2 closest enemies.
Titanic Might is a strong Talent that doubles the power
of Wrecking Ball, especially if your team has access to
burst damage to follow up on your
engage. Throwing 2 enemy Heroes means you will easily
be able to hit both of them with Warlord's Challenge.
When you have Mortal Combo at Level 16
and Titanic Might at Level 20,
when catching 2 enemy Heroes with Wrecking Ball
and hitting them with Groundbreaker right after,
you will be able to throw them on the spot 2 more times.
Unrivaled Strength at Level 1 increases the damage done this way.
You should avoid picking this Talent when your team's strategy involves
killing an isolated enemy Hero using Abilities that split their damage evenly
on all Heroes hit (for example Seven-Sided Strike
by Kharazim).
?
Inner Rage
(Level 20)
Garrosh
Body Check gains an additional charge and its healing reduction is increased by an additional 45%.
Inner Rage is a situational Talent that increases
the value of Body Check by adding a second charge
and empowering the healing reduction component. For obvious reasons, this Talent
can only be picked if Body Check was chosen at Level 1.
Avoid using both charges on the same
enemy Hero in quick succession because, even though healing reduction effects
can stack up to 100% healing reduction, in this case the second application will not stack
with the first one but only refresh its duration.
Pick this Talent when you need healing reduction effects to get kills,
so when the enemy team has enough burst healing
(for example Phase Shift by Brightwing)
to save whoever is being focused by your team.
